verdict.rationale: RustDesk's own docs state that P2P connections use end-to-end encryption based on NaCl, which names the cryptographic primitive library. But the pack has no protocol specification, key-exchange description, or relay-path encryption details, so the 'documented, not just asserted' half of the story is barely met. A hands-on self-hoster also warns that encryption is not enabled by default; this is a deployment caveat rather than proof that encryption fails, so it does not make the claim disputed. Missing for 10: a published protocol/handshake and key-exchange spec, explicit E2E coverage of relayed (non-P2P) sessions, encryption that is on by default in self-hosted setups, and independent audit or verification.

support.subject: As an IT admin, sessions are encrypted end to end with the protocol documented, not just asserted

citations.quote: P2P connection with end-to-end encryption based on NaCl.
